problems.description: get_task_or_404() is misnamed — it returns None instead of raising/returning a 404, and every caller must re-check for None; it is really get_task_or_none.
datetime.utcnow() is deprecated as of Python 3.12; datetime.now(timezone.utc) is preferred.

The 404/400 errorhandler functions are effectively dead code: every route handles bad input and missing tasks itself with task-specific messages, so the registered handlers never fire and add a second, inconsistent error shape.
test_list_tasks_ordered_by_created_at_desc relies on created_at DESC ordering at microsecond resolution; three rapid inserts could tie, making the ordering assertion flaky.

Measured convention score is 0.70 with violations listed in app.py, celery_app.py, celery_config.py and conftest.py; the first three are pre-existing seed files outside this commit's diff, but the conftest.py naming violations are attributable to this commit (third added file, diff truncated).

strengths: Clean Flask app-factory pattern (create_app) with an injectable database path, giving clean test isolation.
Parameterized SQL throughout — no string-interpolated queries, no injection surface.
Comprehensive test suite covering create/list/get/update, 404 and 400 validation paths, and duplicate titles.
Proper Flask idioms: per-request connection via g with teardown_appcontext closing.
commit_reviews.summary: A clean, well-tested greenfield Flask/SQLite task API that follows standard Flask patterns and is largely convention-compliant — the low 0.70 convention score is driven mostly by pre-existing seed files (app.py, celery_app.py, celery_config.py) outside this commit's diff, so the agent's own code grades higher than the measurement suggests.

problems.description: SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded, well-known string 'dev-secret-key' when the env var is unset; with HS256 this makes tokens forgeable if that fallback is ever active in a non-dev environment.
The ALTER TABLE migration adds owner_id as NULL for pre-existing tasks, silently orphaning them — those rows match no user and become permanently invisible with no backfill/reassignment path.
No tests added for the new /auth/register, /auth/login, or owner-scoped /tasks endpoints despite conftest.py existing in the repo.
Registration enforces only a non-empty password (no length policy) and mixed time handling (datetime.utcnow() for created_at vs datetime.now(timezone.utc) for token exp) — minor hygiene gaps.

strengths: Passwords hashed via werkzeug generate_password_hash, never stored in plaintext.
Per-owner scoping applied to every task query, preventing cross-user data leaks.
JWT auth applied uniformly across all /tasks endpoints via a single require_auth decorator.
Graceful migration path for pre-existing databases (PRAGMA + ALTER TABLE) rather than destructive schema reset.
Changed file stays consistent with existing conventions (snake_case functions, UPPER_CASE module constants, same error-format shape).
commit_reviews.summary: Coherent, well-structured feature addition that extends the existing Flask factory pattern with JWT auth and per-user task ownership, though it introduces minor debt via a hardcoded secret fallback, orphaned legacy rows, and untested auth endpoints.

problems.description: tasks_api.py imports celery_app at module import time, so the whole API fails to import if celery is not installed; runtime coupling between the HTTP app and the async transport.

send_notification_email.delay() is unguarded: if the Redis broker is unreachable, the task-update request raises after the DB commit, turning a fire-and-forget notification into a failure point in the request path.

celery_config.py uses lowercase module-level names (broker_url, result_backend, task_serializer...) which the UPPER_CASE lint rule flags; the snake_case is the Celery config convention, but the tension with the project's convention rules is real and unresolvable as written.

The 'Classes should use PascalCase' flags on app.py and conftest.py reference files outside this diff (AST shows +0 classes added), so several listed violations appear to be pre-existing or analyzer false positives — flagging the discrepancy with the 0.70 mechanical score.
Email transport is a print() stub rather than a real delivery mechanism — acceptable for the story context, but the notification system delivers nothing until a real backend is wired in.

strengths: Clean separation of concerns: Celery app and config live in dedicated modules with clear docstrings, keeping tasks_api.py changes minimal.
Graceful schema migration for the new email column (PRAGMA table_info check + ALTER TABLE) so existing databases upgrade in place.
Notification dedupe guard: email only fires on a genuine status transition into 'completed', not on repeat updates.
Solid test coverage (166 lines) exercising explicit email, default email, blank-email rejection, and the mocked trigger path.
Input validation extended consistently for the new email field, matching the existing username/password validation style.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-scoped, testable integration of Celery-based async notifications with a thoughtful DB migration and transition guard, dragged slightly by unguarded broker dispatch and module-level import coupling — with several mechanical convention violations attributable to Celery's snake_case config convention and pre-existing files rather than this diff.

problems.description: BaseRepository exposes generic find_all/update/delete that no caller uses — dead code / speculative generality; update_by_owner bypasses the base update() and hand-rolls SQL instead.
task_repo()/user_repo() closures instantiate a fresh repository on every request rather than caching on g.
BaseRepository interpolates table_name via f-string into SQL. Safe here (class constants), but a fragile pattern if any table name ever becomes dynamic.

Convention score 0.70 reflects violations (PascalCase/snake_case/UPPER_CASE in app.py, celery_app.py, celery_config.py, conftest.py) in files untouched by this commit — the diff's own new code is convention-conformant, so the low score is a pre-existing repo state, not introduced here.

strengths: Clean repository-layer abstraction that removes duplicated raw SQL from all route handlers in tasks_api.py.
Consistently applied to both users and tasks, with owner-scoping preserved on every task query.
Preserves the existing app-factory/closure pattern and keeps parameterized queries throughout.
Reuses the repo in get_task_or_404 and the auth path, collapsing repeated get_db().execute(...).fetchone() boilerplate.
commit_reviews.summary: A sound, consistently-applied repository refactor that removes duplicated raw SQL from route handlers (+1 file, +115/-40, +3 classes) with only minor dead generic methods and per-request instantiation; the 0.70 convention score is driven by pre-existing violations in files outside the diff.

problems.description: GET /tasks response shape changed from a bare JSON array to an envelope {data, next_cursor, total} — a breaking contract for any existing consumer unless all callers/tests were updated in lockstep.
count_by_owner runs a full COUNT(*) per paginated request, giving every page an O(n) scan; this undercuts the constant-cost scaling that cursor pagination is otherwise chosen for.

conftest.py injects fakeredis via storage_options connection_pool; whether Flask-Limiter's redis storage actually honors that kwarg through from_url should be verified, or the tests may silently fall back to in-memory storage and not exercise the real path claimed in the docstring.

Measured convention score 0.70 is driven mostly by violations in files not touched by this diff (app.py, celery_app.py, celery_config.py); the new code itself is snake_case and follows the repository/factory patterns.

strengths: Cursor-based keyset pagination (id < cursor, ORDER BY id DESC, limit+1 has_more, bounded limit validation) is a solid pattern fitting the existing repository layer.
Shared conftest client fixture removes duplicated fixture code from test_notifications.py (-22 lines) and wires the rate limiter to an isolated fake Redis per test.
Per-user rate limiting keyed on JWT user_id with IP fallback, env-configurable limits, and a clean 429 error handler.
New test_pagination.py gives focused coverage of the pagination edge cases (cursor/limit validation, defaults).
commit_reviews.summary: A well-executed cross-cutting session that adds cursor pagination and JWT-keyed rate limiting through the existing factory/repository patterns with shared test fixtures, though the /tasks response-shape change is a breaking contract and the 0.70 convention score mostly reflects pre-existing violations outside this diff.
